text:
matt: Heads up, seeing tiny training pods (0.125-0.5 GPU) stuck Pending in us-west2. Nodes report free GPU but scheduler keeps prebinding to `nvlink-island=true` nodes then failing attach. we end up launching extra spot nodes. cost + latency spike this morning.

sasha: any attach error in events?

matt: one example (abridged):
```
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----    ------            ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled         3m    default-scheduler  Assigned to node-usw2-88
  Warning FailedAttach      3m    attach-detach      AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-xyz": rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded
  Warning FailedScheduling 2m    default-scheduler  Pod failed to fit: 0/40 nodes had available gpu, node(s) had taint: nvlink-island=true:NoSchedule
```

rachel: nvlink-island was added for big-gang locality months ago. probably an affinity rule that biases small pods to those islands to preserve packing for upcoming large runs. looks like the islands are marked NoSchedule but scheduler still attempts prebinds (bad).

deepak: why would scheduler prebind if taint prevents scheduling? sounds like a race between predicate checks and prebind plugin ordering. also volume attach timeouts make it worse — we retry and requeue, spinning the provisioner.

sasha: immediate mitigation options?

matt: shortlist: 1) flip stale island nodes' taint to `PreferNoSchedule` (quick, node-level change) 2) hotpatch scheduler plugin order to evaluate taints earlier than prebind 3) add admission webhook to rewrite affinity for pods <0.5 GPU.

deepak: 1 is risky (breaks large job locality). 3 is heavy. 2 seems safest and reversible. can we do a canary?

matt: plan: patch scheduler-config on canary cluster us-west2-b to evaluate taints as an early filter before prebind. rollout window 20m. monitor: `kube_scheduler_pre_binding_attempts`, `kube_scheduler_failed_scheduling`, and spot instance launch rate. set alert if spot launches > baseline*2 in 10m.

sasha: +1. also add a temporary metric alert for nvlink-island node utilization <10% while tiny-pod pending > 5 for 15m. that shows islands are being reserved but unused.

ops-bot: alert created: ALRT-4021 - us-west2 spot provisioning surge. runbook: /runbooks/spot_scale_surges.md

matt: i'll push the canary patch now. dry-run patch:
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch cm scheduler-config --patch '{"data": {"pluginOrder": "taintFilter, predicates, prebind"}}' --dry-run=client -o yaml
```
I'll open PR, tag @sasha @deepak for expeditious review.

deepak: fyi we should check kubelet attach timeouts too. if attach/detach is flaky then even correct scheduling will thrash. open a follow-up to correlate `attach_detach_controller` logs with pod churn.

matt: canary applied to us-west2-b, observed Pending from 18 -> 4 in 12 minutes. spot launches reduced. attaching screenshot of pod churn chart (uploaded) :thumbsup:

sasha: great. hold 30m then promote if stable. create RFC for small-pod placement policy and long-term fix: controller that ages nvlink-island label and emits `island-owner` annotation.

matt: noted. temporary rollback plan: if pending stays >10 or attach errors persist, revert patch and instead mark orphaned islands `PreferNoSchedule` for small-pod workloads.

ops-bot: note added to incident timeline: INCIDENT-2026NVL - nvlink-affinity-induced spot surge.

rachel: also add cost impact note to the incident: approx +$2.6k over 6h due to extra spot churn (prelim).

sasha: thanks team. please keep logs & events in the ticket for postmortem.
